audit.whatIsWrong: The chart contradicts its own whys on five of seven rows. whys[0] calls level 1 a skill check but the row said Zaahen; whys[2] says 'Level 3 is his' but the row said Skill; whys[4] calls 6 'a wash' but the row said Zaahen; whys[5] and whys[6] both say Zaahen wins first item and two items but the rows said Skill. The packet chart (Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen, Skill, Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen) matches the whys exactly, and the 48.1% win rate over 3089 games supports Zaahen owning the late rows.
audit.why: Both layers agreed with each other, so no mirror check would have caught it — but the page rendered a chart saying Sylas wins first item directly above a sentence saying Zaahen does.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers to match the packet and the whys; ratings rescaled.

audit.why: Four spikes present at Zaahen level 2, Zaahen level 3, your level 6 and Zaahen first item. Timings agree with the corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Zaahen ability is named anywhere on the page — his R is literally called 'Ultimate', including in focus.text, and no cooldown, range or mechanic appears. Three specific interactions are absent: The Darkin Glaive (Q) is an auto-attack reset whose recast knocks up; Aureate Rush (E) is a 10-second dash that deals percent-health damage; and his passive, Determination, lets him revive once filled.
audit.why: The revive is the single most decision-changing fact in the matchup — a Sylas who counts lethal and commits everything can kill him and still lose the fight. The percent-health E means the standard 'buy armour' instinct is wrong, and the Q auto-reset is the tell that his burst has started.
audit.corrected: Grim Deliverance named as the R with its 110-second rank-1 cooldown; Aureate Rush named with its 10-second cooldown and percent-health slice; the Q auto-reset and knockup recast written in; Determination's revive stated in the mid text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is not mentioned anywhere, and wants.foe[1] attributes his sustain to 'his passive'.
audit.why: The healing is on The Darkin Glaive (Q) and Grim Deliverance (R); the passive grants attack damage and the revive, not healing. Anti-heal is what decides the extended brawl the page tells you to avoid.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] repointed at Q and R, and Grievous Wounds made an explicit want in wants.you[2].

notes: This page named none of Zaahen's abilities — his ultimate was written as the literal word 'Ultimate' in focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns and six report/dos/donts fields.
